rationale_evidence.statement: Argues a conventional document structure (ADR files, standards.md) cannot answer relationship questions like 'which service implements ADR-002' or 'which evidence proves it is satisfied,' hence KnowledgeOS needs graph-like semantics even if its physical persistence is not a graph database; presents the complete simplified graph (Business Intent->Governance Decision->Authoritative Knowledge->Architecture/Policy Rule->Expected State-comparedWith->Observed Runtime State->Evidence->Verification->{PASS,FAIL->Finding->Governance->New Decision}).

- [S1029] types=[FORMALIZATION, HYPOTHESIS] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Opens Step 130 (KnowledgeOS Assurance Graph): combines all derived objects (knowledge, claims, evidence, authority, decisions, policies, observations, findings, recommendations, actions, verification, fitness rules, agents, runtime, governance) into one target graph Intent->Decision->Knowledge->Rule->Implementation->Runtime->Evidence->Verification->Finding->Governance, reframing the question from 'what objects exist?' to 'can we traverse the complete lifecycle of an engineering decision from organizational intent all the way to runtime evidence and back?' — calling the resulting construct, if machine-traversable, 'the central architectural construct around which the rest of the platform can be organized.'" (anchor: "Intent → Decision → Knowledge → Rule → Implementation → Runtime → Evidence → Verification → Finding → Governance")
- [S1030] types=[ARGUMENT] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Argues a conventional document structure (ADR files, standards.md) cannot answer relationship questions like 'which service implements ADR-002' or 'which evidence proves it is satisfied,' hence KnowledgeOS needs graph-like semantics even if its physical persistence is not a graph database; presents the complete simplified graph (Business Intent->Governance Decision->Authoritative Knowledge->Architecture/Policy Rule->Expected State-comparedWith->Observed Runtime State->Evidence->Verification->{PASS,FAIL->Finding->Governance->New Decision})." (anchor: "Which production service implements ADR-002? Which evidence proves that ADR-002 is still satisfied?")
- [S1030] types=[FORMALIZATION, DISTINCTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Distinguishes the Intent flow (Why->What->How, giving forward traceability: business requirement->architecture decision->constraint->implementation requirement->code/config->deployment) from the Evidence flow (what happened->what proves it->does it conform->what should change, giving backward traceability: runtime->observation->evidence->verification->finding->governance); states ForwardTraceability+BackwardTraceability is a core KnowledgeOS capability." (anchor: "Why → What → How ... What happened → What proves it → Does it conform? → What should change?")
- [S1030] types=[EXAMPLE] scope=OBJECT — "Worked graph example: D42->K17->R11->ServiceA->ContractX, then ContractX->O88->E91->V12=PASS, letting the system state 'ADR-42 is currently implemented and verified through evidence E-91'; contrasting failed case — runtime uses contract Y instead, Expected=X vs Observed=Y, V12=FAIL, Finding F31, representing architectural drift explicitly in the graph." (anchor: "ADR-42 is currently implemented and verified through evidence E-91.")
- [S1030] types=[FORMALIZATION, DISTINCTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Redefines Drift as a graph difference (stronger than document comparison) and enumerates five drift levels: Structural (dependency differs), Behavioral (runtime behavior differs), Governance (implementation bypasses an approved decision), Temporal (knowledge is stale), Evidence (expected evidence is missing); reiterates Drift ≠ Violation since an ApprovedException may explain the difference, giving EffectiveExpectedState = BaseArchitecture + ApplicableExceptions and Drift = EffectiveExpectedState - ObservedState, illustrated by an exception graph (Architecture Decision->Expected State A -exception-> Exception E17 -> Effective State B -> Runtime State B)." (anchor: "Drift = Difference(ExpectedGraph, ObservedGraph).")
- [S1030] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=OBJECT — "Catalogs six graph-query patterns with their traversals: 'why' (ServiceX->Configuration->Decision->Rationale->BusinessIntent, causal/intent traceability), 'who authorized' (Configuration->Action->Authorization->Authority), 'what proves it' (Knowledge->Verification->Evidence), 'what changed' (KnowledgeVersion_n->n+1, Decision->ImplementationChange->Deployment), 'what is affected' (Decision->Knowledge->Systems->Components->Deployments, impact analysis), 'what becomes invalid' when D42 is superseded (D42->Knowledge->Rules->Verification->AffectedSystems, enabling targeted re-verification)." (anchor: "Why? Who? What proves it? What changed? What is affected? What becomes invalid?")
- [S1030] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Proposes dependency-aware selective verification (rather than re-running every check after every change) as a potential major efficiency improvement, worked with an example where a ServiceA change identifies only Rules R1/R7/R19 as relevant; lists impact-graph relationship types needed for traversal: affects, dependsOn, implements, governs, verifiedBy." (anchor: "Change → AffectedGraph → RelevantRules → RunOnlyRelevantVerification.")
- [S1030] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Reapplies the traceability-strength scale T0-T4 to the Decision->Implementation edge specifically, listing possible evidence kinds (architecture reference, repository metadata, PR, commit, deployment artifact, test, runtime observation) so a governance dashboard can distinguish weak from strong traceability." (anchor: "T0=No link ... T4=Verified.")
- [S1030] types=[DEFINITION, DISTINCTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Distinguishes the model from a conventional 'knowledge graph' (entities+relationships) by adding Authority, Evidence, TemporalValidity, EpistemicStatus, Verification, proposing the more precise term 'Assurance Graph' since it is explicitly designed to establish trustworthy relationships — illustrated by contrasting a generic 'Service A depends on Service B' with an assurance-graph answer naming the governing decision, commit, deployment, verifying rule, and timestamp." (anchor: "Assurance Graph")
- [S1030] types=[DISTINCTION, FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "States not all graph nodes are equally authoritative (node-level epistemic status must be preserved) and extends this to edges: even relationships (e.g. ServiceA -ownedBy-> TeamX) should ideally be evidence-backed, giving evidence-backed edges (Service A -ownedBy[Evidence E17]-> Team X) so the graph becomes explainable ('why does the system believe Team X owns Service A?' traverses OwnershipClaim->Evidence) rather than generated from LLM intuition." (anchor: "AgentRecommendation may have EpistemicStatus=INFERRED while ArchitectureDecision may have Authority=ArchitectureBoard.")
- [S1030] types=[EXAMPLE, PRINCIPLE] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Defines the agent's graph role as Navigate + Interpret + Recommend (not Invent + Remember + Declare), worked with an agent query D42->K->Rules->Services for impact analysis; KnowledgeOS supplies the authoritative graph rather than the agent inventing structure." (anchor: "Find all services affected by the supersession of Decision D42.")
- [S1030] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Defines task-scoped context retrieval as a subgraph G_task ⊆ G_KOS (the semantic equivalent of context retrieval), worked with a Nexus-migration context subgraph (Nexus -governedBy-> D17, -currentState-> O81, -deployedAs-> A92, -verifiedBy-> R44, -exception-> E12, -finding-> F31); argues sending a RelevantSubgraph rather than thousands of documents should improve agent reasoning because context is authoritative, relevant, provenance-aware, and temporally valid." (anchor: "G_task = Relevant(Task, Authority, Knowledge, Evidence, CurrentState) ⊆ G_KOS.")
- [S1030] types=[FORMALIZATION, PRINCIPLE] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Defines a graph-based retrieval pipeline Task->Anchor->Traversal->Subgraph->AgentContext as fundamentally different from pure semantic search, but argues semantic search remains useful as a first pass (SemanticSearch->CandidateKnowledge, then graph traversal establishes RelevantRelationships), concluding SemanticRetrieval+GraphTraversal is stronger than either alone, and sketching a hybrid retrieval architecture (User Task -> {Semantic Search->Candidate Nodes, Graph Traversal} -> Relevant Subgraph -> Agent Context) as a likely direction for the AI engineering platform." (anchor: "Task → Anchor → Traversal → Subgraph → AgentContext.")
- [S1030] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Requires the graph to distinguish Current from Historical (a retrieval system returning superseded knowledge unmarked can produce dangerous agent decisions) and supports temporal graph queries Traverse(G,t) enabling 'what did we believe at that time'; extends this to audit reconstruction — given Action=A81, reconstruct Context(t_A81) to answer what knowledge/decisions/exceptions/evidence/authorization were applicable when the agent acted, a 'true AI audit trail,' worked as an action-reconstruction chain (A81 -executedBy-> Agent, -authorizedBy-> Authorization, -basedOn-> Context C42, -proposedBy-> Recommendation R17, -verifiedBy-> Verification V88), argued to be substantially more defensible than storing only an agent transcript." (anchor: "Traverse(G,t=now) vs Traverse(G,t=2025-06-01).")
- [S1030] types=[HYPOTHESIS, FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "States the stronger hypothesis that the Assurance Graph should be KnowledgeOS's semantic backbone, with documents/APIs/dashboards/agent contexts/reports as projections over it (Assurance Graph -> {Documents->Humans, APIs->Systems, Agent Context->Agents}); explicitly qualifies this as GraphSemantics as an architectural requirement, not a mandate to 'implement a graph database' — physical persistence (relational/document/graph/event-sourced/hybrid) is a later decision depending on query patterns, consistency requirements, scale, and existing architecture; DDD comes before technology selection." (anchor: "The Assurance Graph should become the semantic backbone of KnowledgeOS.")
- [S1030] types=[DISTINCTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Defines Memory = Relationships+Evidence+Authority+Time as organizational memory, contrasting an LLM's 'I remember we discussed Nexus' with KnowledgeOS's 'Decision D17 governs Nexus migration, approved by X, effective Y, active, supported by evidence E42' (LLM memory ≠ organizational memory); uses this to validate the .claude/.codex local-memory-vs-KnowledgeOS-authority principle — local harness memory stores workflow preferences/session context/operational hints/temporary state (Convenience), KnowledgeOS stores authoritative knowledge/evidence/governance/decisions (Authority)." (anchor: "LLM memory ≠ Organizational memory.")
- [S1030] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "States relationships need epistemic status too (Confidence, Evidence, Source, Status — e.g. 'Service A implements Decision D42, Status:VERIFIED, Evidence:E91, Verified:2026-08-28') to prevent hallucinated topology: an LLM-inferred relationship becomes only a CandidateRelationship (AgentInference->CandidateRelationship->Verification->VerifiedRelationship->Governance->AuthoritativeRelationship), giving relationships their own epistemic lifecycle Candidate->Supported->Verified->Authoritative->Superseded." - [S1030] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXAMPLE] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Defines TraceabilityCompleteness TC(D) for a governed decision D, worked example — D42 requires authority/rationale/affected-systems/implementation/verification, 4/5 verified gives TC=80%, but if the missing relationship is Authority the decision may still be invalid despite high completeness, so Criticality must complement completeness (echoing WeightedCompleteness from S1021); lists six Assurance Graph health dimensions (AuthorityIntegrity, ProvenanceCompleteness, TraceabilityCompleteness, TemporalValidity, VerificationCoverage, AgentActionTraceability) as more meaningful than a generic 'knowledge quality score.'"
